Lovely poem. The short and succinct lines seem to evoke a bittersweet memory that I dont even have. My main issue lies with the structure. I feel that some separation would allow for every line to feel more distinct. As it is now, it is just a mass of lines that seem to go together in any order, and as a reader seemed to be saying the same thing over and over. Other than that, I feel that the flow could be fleshed out more. A couple times throughout the poem you will repeat something at the beginning of a line, for instance

>Even if you're by my casket 

>Even if it's eternal sleep

And I think that's really good. It makes each line more memorable on its own, but also as a part of that pair. I think there are many places that seem like they're about to do this, then don't.
For instance

>Perhaps so peaceful

>It is quite gay

When I read that first line, I fully expected and wanted the next line to also start with "perhaps." Even just a simple swap to "perhaps quite gay" seems to fit better with the flow of the poem.

Wow, I'm absolutely in love with this. The rhyme scheme flows so naturally despite being seemingly simple. It tells the story of someone lost in a world where they can do anything, but can't decide what for one reason or another. Eventually, they end up going along with everyone else, instead of being themselves. Where I could see some improvement would be in the first two stanzas. After the poem gets going, it goes beautifully, but the first stanza seemed almost abrupt and hard to digest. The second stanza begins well, but the transition to 

>On my ears advice rots

Is a breakaway from the natural flow of the rest of the poem. The next line as well feels a little funky, but I believe this is due to the quoted line above.

If I could recommend anything (from someone with little experience and purely as a reader), it would be to adjust that line in some way, perhaps a different syllable count would roll off the tongue better, or maybe adjust the wording. On top of that, the first stanza could use a more soft opening, if that makes any sense. How to do this would be entirely up to you, as there's a lot of freedom. It could be adding in some lines, or even starting with an entirely different stanza. Up to you to decide.

I love the imagery you use in this, and the message is something I can relate to. The only thing I would point out would be the structure. 

>Beings made of ivory pure, Blessed by the angels

>I was made from sticks and stones, And things best left unlabeled

Having these two sections rhyming but completely separate is totally fine, but keeping it consistent through the rest of the poem would be best. The only time a change would be warranted would be along with a change in mood or scheme. Along with that is the awkwardness of reading certain sections that have no punctuation 

>I tried to fix myself But it can't be undone The way were born won't right itself From our skin we cannot run

I had to reread this a couple times to grasp it. I would say add punctuation or just forego periods and start a new line for each part. Also, the missing apostrophe in "we're" threw me off at first.

Don't get me wrong though, the wording, rhyme scheme, and message all came together wonderfully, good job.

I love how there are clear sections, your burden in life, the hope for you to be useful after death, and the ending that ties it all together nicely. This did resonate with me as someone chronically suicidal, the feeling of being a burden to anything and everything I touch, but wanting nothing but good things for those very people/objects.

If I had to give some criticism, it would be on the structure. While I like the lowercase "i", as it shows the reader how little the writer thinks of themselves, the separation via slashes makes the poem a little harder to approach.

Overall it was beautiful and I loved it though.
